codes.name: Days arranged round the dog
codes.description: Times, routes and rooms set by what the dog needs, often noticed only once they are in place.

codes.name: Rules nobody wrote down
codes.description: Routines and rules between person and dog that grew up without being agreed in words.

codes.name: Who does the dog's work
codes.description: Who gets up, walks and carries the care, and what that says between the people in the house.

codes.name: A reason to get up
codes.description: The dog's needs giving a morning a shape it lacked, or the lack of one once the dog has gone.

codes.name: A house filled or emptied by the dog
codes.description: The dog as what makes a house feel lived in, felt most when the dog is out of it.

codes.name: The dog as a reason nobody argues with
codes.description: The dog given as the reason for being somewhere, or not, which other people accept without question.

codes.name: Talking to the dog
codes.description: Speaking to the dog out loud, as to a person, about the day or about nothing.

codes.name: The dog as a way round hard talk
codes.description: The dog standing in for, or interrupting, talk that people find hard with each other.

codes.name: Doubts kept unsaid
codes.description: Doubts or regrets about the dog that are felt and kept back from the people nearest.

codes.name: Wanted without conditions
codes.description: The dog's welcome felt as asking for nothing, with nothing that has to have been got right.

codes.name: The dog in a person's place
codes.description: The dog taking a place, a role or a habit that a person once held.

codes.name: A life opening out
codes.description: New people, places and habits that came with the dog.

codes.name: A life closing in
codes.description: A life narrowing round the dog's needs: fewer outings, fewer people, fewer yeses.

codes.name: Caring for myself through the dog
codes.description: Looking after the dog bringing looking after oneself with it: meals, exercise, a quiet head.

codes.name: Keeping watch
codes.description: Alertness on the dog's behalf, for its safety or for others', that does not switch off.

codes.name: Rehearsing the dog's death
codes.description: Imagining the dog's illness or death ahead of time, and being caught out by how much it hurts.

codes.name: Settling the dog's future
codes.description: Deciding where the dog will live and with whom, by rehoming it or by a will.

codes.name: Others judging the dog's place
codes.description: Family, neighbours or landlords questioning whether the dog should stay, and answering them.

codes.name: Asking whether it was my fault
codes.description: Asking whether the dog's troubles, or its going, were the person's own doing.

codes.name: Loss without a name yet
codes.description: Missing a dog that is still alive elsewhere, a feeling the speaker cannot yet name.

codes.name: The dog's joy lifting a mood
codes.description: The dog's pleasure taking a bad mood away, sometimes before the person is ready to let it go.

codes.name: Two feelings at once
codes.description: Holding opposite feelings about the same thing at once, and saying so.
